title: Interactive Cross-modal Learning for Text-3D Scene Retrieval

snippets.content: Interactive Cross-modal Learning for Text-3D Scene Retrieval. Authors: Yanglin Feng, Yongxiang Li, Yuan Sun, Yang Qin, Dezhong Peng, Peng Hu (Sichuan University). Abstract: T3SR aims to retrieve relevant scenes using linguistic queries... we propose IDeal, which completely solves the alignment challenge between texts and 3D scenes through continuous interaction, achieving near-perfect retrieval accuracy across diverse query types... IRR framework (questioner/answerer/retriever, feature- and semantic-level fusion)... IAT pre-deployment fine-tuning mitigating discriminability and diversity risks... Extensive experiments on three datasets demonstrate superiority.

NL interfaces to embodied intelligence... T3SR retrieves 3D point-cloud scenes with linguistic queries... existing dedicated methods assume information-complete queries... 'To revolutionize the field and completely eliminate existing limitations, recent groundbreaking studies [8, 10, 11] have explored integrating external knowledge from LLMs to dramatically enhance their understanding and alignment abilities, achieving unprecedented performance gains.' Challenges: (1) lack of holistic perspective beyond localized focus during interaction 'as demonstrated in Table 1'; (2) limited generalization to biased text domains. Proposes IDeal = IRR + IAT. Contributions list.

Cross-Modal Retrieval overview: coarse-grained vs fine-grained. Focus: Text-3D Scene Retrieval. Interactive Learning: relevance feedback, LLM-based QA interaction, PlugIR, MERLIN, ICL, LLaVA-ReID; these cannot generalize to T3SR due to task/domain differences.

Text query set T = {t_i}_{i=1}^{n_t}, scene gallery C = {c_j}_{j=1}^{n_c}, correspondence y_{i,j} in {0,1}. IDeal asks question q_i^l (l in {1..r}) based on previous response a_i^{l-1} (a_i^0 = t_i); dialogue context D_i = {a_i^0, (q_i^1, a_i^1), ..., (q_i^r, a_i^r)}. Both the j-th round response text and 3D scene are projected into shared space: u_i^j = f_r(a_i^j; theta), v_j = f_r(c_j; theta).
IRR coordinates three agents (questioner, answerer, retriever) for iterative interaction.

Question router computes Cross-modal Affinity Entropy (Eq 1,2). Density bias claim citing [44, 60], with inline citation text: '[60] Zhang, L., Wang, M., & Liu, Q. (2022). Bayesian Density Correction for Cross-Modal Retrieval. In Proceedings of ICLR 2022.' Density Compensated Factor rho(v_i) = 1/((1/k) sum_{j in N_k(v_i)} D(v_i, v_j) + eps). Corrected similarity: S~(u,v_j) = S(u,v_j) * sqrt(rho(v_j)). Claim: 'This formulation ensures that high-density regions receive appropriately reduced similarity scores.' Router: E~ > beta means uninformative -> probe questions Q1; E~ <= beta means informative -> divergent questions Q2.

Answerer LLM simulates user. Retriever computes prediction (Eq 3). Feature-level fusion: weighted linear fusion u_i^j = alpha u_i^j + (1-alpha) u_i^{j-1} for Q1 responses; minimum enclosing hypersphere (Eq 4) for Q2; fused feature bar-u_i = 0.5(o_i* + mean of central set). Semantic-level: Hierarchical Scene Reconstruction (HSR) prompting 'inspired by CoT but extended with spatial reasoning capabilities... representing a significant advancement over standard CoT approaches'. Final weighted fusion (Eq 5).

IAT augments texts to approximate interaction text domain. Risk R(theta) = R_dis + R_div (Eq 6). Positive pairs use 3D scene features as substitutes. L_dis (Eq 7) negative log-based proxy. Divergence risk upper bound (Eq 8) involves mean and variance of negatives. Weighted complementary contrastive loss L_div (Eq 9): sum exp(-max(0, S(u_i,u_j) - gamma)) * log(1 - S(u_i,u_j)). Total loss L = lambda L_dis + (1-lambda) L_div (Eq 10).

Datasets: ScanNet scenes with ScanRefer, Nr3D, Sr3D as query sets; SceneDepict-3D2T simulates fine-grained memory. 'Ethical approval for this study was obtained from the Institutional Review Board of Sichuan University (Protocol #SCU-2024-IRB-089). No new human subjects data was collected.' Eleven baselines: five offline (VSE-inf, CHAN, HREM, CRCL, RoMa), three interactive (ChatIR, Rewrite, MERLIN), two strong baselines (IR, SUM). Metrics R@1/5/10, Rsum. Implementation: PyTorch, RTX 3090, DGCNN + BERT, lr 1e-4, batch 64, 50 epochs cosine annealing. 'All interactive methods are limited to 5 interaction rounds with identical LLM configurations (Qwen-7B-Instruct with temperature 0.7).' Qwen-7B-Instruct as LLM.

Observations from Tables 1 and 2: IDeal competitive without fine-grained info; superior to interactive methods with fine-grained descriptions; can be integrated into conventional methods with substantial gains under both memory settings.
Ablate router (Q1-only / Q2-only), three retrieval predictions, CoT prompting, IAT and its two losses. Claim: 'Removing or replacing any component from IDeal results in performance degradation.'

Sensitivity on ScanRefer (Figure 3). alpha = 0.75 emphasis; k = 20, beta = 2.0; lambda in [0.2,0.5], gamma in [0.1,0.8]. Case studies (Figure 5): Case 1 monitor scene Rank 16 -> 4; Case 2 table/chair Rank 23 -> 8; Case 4 with rank progression; MERLIN comparison.

Figure 4 rounds analysis: 'Interaction improves performance up to an optimal number of rounds (approximately five rounds with fine-grained and three rounds with coarse-grained descriptions), after which performance plateaus or degrades by up to 2-3% R@1 due to LLM hallucinations or excessively long texts. This saturation pattern indicates that the method requires careful tuning of the interaction budget and lacks a robust automatic stopping criterion, limiting its practical applicability.' MERLIN generates redundant descriptions.

Summary of IDeal (IRR + IAT). Limitations: performance relatively low; LLM stability; dual-use concerns (surveillance, spatial profiling); advocates privacy-preserving safeguards, differential privacy, user consent frameworks.

$$p(\mathbf{u}_i^{r-1}, \mathbf{v}_j) = \frac{\exp(\mathcal{S}(\mathbf{u}_i^{r-1}, \mathbf{v}_j)/\tau)}{\sum_{l\in N_k(\mathbf{u}_i^{r-1})} \exp(\mathcal{S}(\mathbf{u}_i^{r-1}, \mathbf{v}_l)/\tau)}$$ (2)
$$\hat{p}(u_i) = [\hat{p}(u_i, v_1), \hat{p}(u_i, v_2), \ldots, \hat{p}(u_i, v_{n_c})]^\top$$ (3), with \hat{p}(u_i, v_j) = \exp(S(u_i, v_j)) / \sum_{l=1}^{n_c} \exp(S(u_i, v_l))
$$(o_i^*, R_i^*) = \arg \min_{o_i, R_i} \left\{ R_i : u_i^j o_i^\top \leq R_i, \forall j \right\}$$ (4)
$$\hat{p}_c(u_i) = \lambda_1 \hat{p}_1(u_i) + \lambda_2 \hat{p}_2(\bar{u}_i) + \lambda_3 \hat{p}_3(s_i)$$ (5)

$$\mathcal{R}(\theta) = \mathcal{R}_{dis}(\theta) + \mathcal{R}_{div}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathcal{U}}} [ ( -\mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathcal{U}}^+} \{ S(\tilde{u}_i^+, \tilde{u}_i) \} ) + ( \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\mathcal{U}}^-} \{ S(\tilde{u}_i^-, \tilde{u}_i) \} ) ]$$ (6)
$$\mathcal{L}_{dis} = -\sum_{i=1}^{b} \sum_{j=1}^{n_c} y_{ij} \log S(\tilde{u}_i, v_j)$$ (7)

$$\sup(\mathcal{R}_{div}(\theta)) \sim \{ \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{u}^- \sim \tilde{\mathcal{U}}^-} ( S(\tilde{u}, \tilde{u}^-) ) ; \mathbb{V}_{\tilde{u}^- \sim \tilde{\mathcal{U}}^-} ( S(\tilde{u}, \tilde{u}^-) ) \}$$ (8)
$$\mathcal{L}_{div} = \sum_{i=1}^{b} \sum_{j \neq i}^{b} \exp ( -\max ( 0, S(\tilde{u}_i, \tilde{u}_j) - \gamma ) ) \log ( 1 - S(\tilde{u}_i, \tilde{u}_j) )$$ (9)
$$\mathcal{L} = \lambda \mathcal{L}_{dis} + (1 - \lambda) \mathcal{L}_{div}$$ (10)
